column3: §FILM_FACT sheets / pile_w / pile_h / plan_gap · stage 0 of the raw set · FILM_DXF2BIM_WHY_MARKINGS.md w01
column4: M: {sheets} drawings, exactly as drawn. No building yet.
column5: M: A common BricsCAD set: {sheets} drawings, exactly as drawn. | F: Where is the building? | M: There is none yet. Each sheet is its own flat world, one drawing unit is one millimetre. The pile spreads {pile_w} by {pile_h} metres, and the floor plan and the foundation plan sit {plan_gap} metres apart.

column3: §FILM_FACT sheets / steps / phase1 / phase2 / phase3 · start of the play on open
column4: M: Three passes over all {sheets} sheets: scale, orient, assemble.
column5: M: Now the system fills in what the drawings leave unsaid, in three passes over all {sheets} sheets. | F: How many steps? | M: {steps}. First every sheet is scaled to metres: {phase1} steps. Then each is oriented: {phase2}. Then they are assembled one after another onto the plan grid: {phase3}. The card at the bottom names the sheet and what was done to it.

column3: §FILM_FACT level_steps / level_value · the LEVEL steps of the play
column4: M: No plan states a level. Level {level_value}, in orange.
column5: M: {level_steps} plans state no level, and no title names a storey. | F: So what level do they get? | M: Level {level_value}, the ground, shown in orange. Orange is an inference, not a reading: you can type over it.

column3: §FILM_FACT play_s / tinted / tinted_inferred · after the play
column4: M: {tinted} sheets are tinted: placed by values not yet yours.
column5: M: {steps} steps in {play_s} seconds. {tinted} sheets are tinted, placed by values that are not yours yet, and {tinted_inferred} of them carry an orange inference. | F: Is anything written to the files? | M: Nothing. It is a view of what the drawings would become.

column3: §FILM_FACT open_yellow_rows / open_blocking / after_accept_blocking · Accept all, then Convert
column4: M: Accept all makes the yellow yours. Convert still refuses.
column5: M: Accept all makes the yellow yours: {open_yellow_rows} rows, and none left. | F: Can it convert now? | M: No. {open_blocking} items blocked it before, and {after_accept_blocking} still do. The list names each one. What the drawing does not say, it does not invent.

column3: §FILM_FACT second_z / heights_typed / tinted_after · the height question and the second heights typed
column4: M: The panel asks for a second height, outlined in red.
column5: M: A height is the one thing a drawing cannot default. The panel asks for it, and outlines the empty fields in red. | F: What does it ask? | M: One height is known: the ground. Give a second: read a level text or a dimension on the sheet, type it in metres, and the y where it is drawn. Here {second_z} metres, on {heights_typed} sheets. {tinted_after} sheets are still tinted.

column3: §FILM_FACT processed_replays / processed_skip_on_open / processed_blocking · the processed set opens
column4: M: The processed set opens placed. No replay.
column5: M: The same set, now processed: its markings are inside the drawings. | F: Does the morph play again? | M: No. {processed_replays} replays; it opens already placed. The morph is for raw drawings: it shows what was before, so you remember it after.

column3: §FILM_FACT converted.n / n_columns / n_beams / n_footings / n_walls · Convert of the processed set, floor slab and roof ticked
column4: M: Convert, with the floor slab and roof ticked: {converted.n} bodies.
column5: M: Convert, with the floor slab and the roof ticked: they are amber, estimated from the drawing's own evidence plus stated conventions. {converted.n} bodies: {n_columns} columns, {n_beams} beams, {n_footings} footings, {n_walls} walls, and the members between. One shed, from nine flat drawings.

column4: F: What was not shown? | M: Listed on the card.
column5: F: What was not shown? | M: Listed on the card. The layer types, body heights and roof were stated by the command line for the processed set, not typed here. And these are a client's drawings, so the set is not published.

column4: M: Nine drawings. One shed. Nothing invented.
column5: M: Nine drawings, one shed, and nothing invented.
